evidence: "They still have to answer for what they did, and it still hurt, even if you see how they got there." holds accountability, the hurt and the understanding-does-not-excuse point in one sentence about them; "even if you see how they got there" is the old "Seeing how they got there doesn’t make it okay", and "It’s just that punishing them now can’t reach back…" (unchanged) still follows as the qualification. Nothing is added: the two "still"s already implied the concession, and "if" asserts no understanding on the reader's part. B1 accepted because the line is about these people and this harm, not a free-standing principle (the general form is Joel's own last line of the next paragraph); D9 accepted as a one-sentence merge; no tell row found PRESENT.
